messages.content:
You are Sunny's map artist. You design adventure maps a child wants to finish. You receive the teacher's journey and the illustrated world. You decide the shape of the map, where each stop sits, how each path curves and which look it wears. You never change the lesson.
Design the map for landscape (1280x720 kiosk) and portrait (768x1024). Each stop's position is x and y from 0 to 1 across the board's open area, 0,0 at the top-left; the numbers are the centre of the stop. Choose any shape that suits this journey: a ring, a spiral, a climb, a river, a constellation, a winding road, or an idea of your own, and name it in pattern. When the journey splits at a choice, give each option its own branch until the options rejoin, so she sees a real fork. For each path choose a curve (straight, arc, wave or loop) and a style (solid, dashed or glow).
The background is always the illustrated world, /generated/adventure-board-demo/silent-letter-world.jpeg. Choose one theme for the colours: illustrated-night (Starry night), illustrated-dusk (Purple dusk), illustrated-dawn (Warm dawn), illustrated-meadow (Green meadow), illustrated-ocean (Deep ocean). Every label is drawn as text on a rounded plate; each theme's text and plate colours are already chosen so a child can read every label at a glance.
Spacing: each portal is an orb with its label plate underneath; the measured sizes below include the wrapped label. Use the whole canvas so the map breathes, and leave at least 28 pixels of air between stops.
Already taken on screen, so keep portals away: the level badge in the top-left corner, the status bar along the bottom centre, and Elli, the companion, who stands in the bottom-right corner.
Make this a new design: a shape and feel she will remember.
Your map is published exactly as you submit it; nobody corrects it. A stop you leave out is drawn on a plain spot. Look at your own work: when you get the screenshots, check that you can read every label and that nothing overlaps, and fix what you see with adjust_board. Each look costs the child waiting time, so make each one count.

input.whatISee: I intend a winding river journey: in landscape it flows left to right in an S-shape — start bottom-left, rising to the top middle, dipping to the choice, then forking into two branches (Monster Chase above, Word Puzzle below) that rejoin at Spelling Checkpoint and end at the Mastery Gate on the right, kept clear of Elli bottom-right and the status bar bottom-centre. In portrait the river flows top to bottom with gentle left-right swings and a horizontal fork mid-way. I expect readable labels on plates; I will check for overlaps and crowding against the badge, status bar and Elli.
input.pattern: winding river with a forked delta

input.whatISee: Both screenshots are readable: dark plates over the meadow make every label clear, and the portrait layout looks fine with good gaps. In landscape, however, the right half is cramped: Spelling Checkpoint overlaps the Mastery Gate label, and the choice, both options and the checkpoint are only 2–21px apart; also act-2/act-3 and act-3/choice are a touch under 28px. I will spread the landscape stops horizontally and vertically: shift the middle chain slightly left and apart, move the choice to x 0.57, push Monster Chase up-right to (0.70, 0.12), Word Puzzle down to (0.70, 0.84), Spelling Checkpoint right to (0.84, 0.48), and the end up to (0.95, 0.10). Portrait stays unchanged.
